LESSON: DRAWING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.3: Drawing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Drawing, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: What tools are used in drawing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign vocabulary of lines related to drawing (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify straight, wavy, zigzag lines (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. draw lines in different position, (

   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. draw patterns using line, (

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Drawing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner draws different lines and create texture on the drawn shapes,

• Communication: The learner speaks clearly, mentioning lines found in the environment.

Values:
• Unity: The learner cooperatively works with others in making pattern formations.

• Responsibility: The learner cares for resources as they source appropriate materials for drawing such as coloured pencils, crayons,

charcoal

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health promotion: The learner observes hygiene by properly washing hands after rubbing to simulate texture on found objects in the

environment.

Link to other learning areas:

• Mathematical Activities: The learner applies the line drawing skills acquired in Mathematics to draw various lines in the environment.

• Environmental Activities: The learner names various lines in their environment.

Open safe quite space, digital devices: laptops, tablets, phones, computers colour pencils, crayons, charcoal, reference books, flash cards
